But... hehe.
Things like this aren't a burden to me at all.
...So, please... don't be afraid either.
...I feel someone's gaze on me.

—Summer training camp. Naturally, I end up spending
far more time with Still in Love than usual, but...

Still in Love simply smiled as she always did,
answering casually as though it were nothing at all.
Ah...

.........
...I... told you before that I wanted to change myself, didn't I?

(...Hehe, you jumped.
Did the sand brushing against your feet tickle?)

...Yet, you made me believe...
that I was fine just the way I was. So, at the very least...

I brought Still in Love a short distance away from the camp lodge.
There was a small, open clearing surrounded by trees.

Her voice—not that of "the other girl"—carried no hint of madness.
It merely melted quietly into the sound of the rolling waves.
...Huh?

I-I'm sorry. Look at me...
I was staring far too much... It made you uncomfortable, didn't it...?

Anytime, anywhere, no matter the moment—
I find myself watching Still in Love.
Things that are fun, things that are unusual.
To think that you... would do something like that, for me...

Her enchanting tone leaves me slightly bewildered.
Unaware of my confusion, she simply giggles softly.

...I don't mind. If it's you who is calling for me,
then surely... it is precious time that I need, too...
What truly... beautiful stars.
(Even if... I were to be scolded for being shameless...)

(Trainer... getting to know you makes me happy.
So, so happy...)
So please, call for me.
...—Show me... moooore...

(My gentle Trainer... please don't hide anything. I want to know more.
Every part of you, down to your very depths...)

...I was worried that my actions... and the way I am...
might become a burden to you, Trainer...

...Hehe. Is that so?
Well then... I suppose it can't be helped.

For an instant, heat flares in her eyes. I wonder if it's "the other girl," but it isn't.
Still completely herself, she weaves her words.
I'm looking at you, Trainer...

Still in Love shifts flusteredly,
her eyes darting as if gauging my reaction.

(...Ah. You're walking ahead along the path I'm to take.
Slowly, checking every step beneath your feet...)

I want to see the same sights together, eat delicious food together;
I find myself thinking that way, and sometimes I even speak it aloud.
And then, as if making up her mind, she began to speak.

(Even though it must be draining your stamina...
you watch over my training with a smile, not letting it show on your face at all...)
...More...
...So pretty...

(What color is the sky you love the most?
...I want to know. I want to know so desperately.)

I've never once felt burdened, but what matters is how she feels.
If doing this puts her mind at ease—
(—...Still.)

Yes... But I'm not afraid.
As long as I'm with you, no matter what path it is...
...Everything I discover about you is so precious, so endearing...

(You're staring at a fallen seashell... Do you like it?
Or are you worried someone might step on it and get hurt?)

(Are you good at swimming? Or not so good? ...Either is fine.
As long as I can be by your side, even on the sandy beach—... Ah, a wave.)

Every time our eyes meet, Still in Love smiles happily.
Unable to contain my curiosity about her gaze any longer, I asked her about it.

...Trainer.
Shall we head back soon?

I looked up at the starry sky once more. Dazzled by its overwhelming glow,
I failed to notice the crimson gaze fixed upon the side of my face—

(...Do you not do well in the heat, I wonder?
You're... sweating so much.)

I asked her if this wasn't too much of a burden.
Still in Love looked momentarily dumbfounded, and then—

It wasn't just places. Whenever I found something pleasant,
I wanted to share it with Still in Love.

To put it in the extreme—it felt as though she was wishing
for me to place an equal burden upon her.

(I wanted to accept every single part of you,
so I searched for the sides of yourself you'd want to hide, and yet—)

A sea of stars unlike anything you could see in the city. Thanks to being away
from the camp lodge and other buildings, only the starlight floats in the sky.
...Won't you bare... even more to me someday?

I was simply captivated without thinking...
Um, this starry sky... looks just like Trainer's... well...

(—You look up at the sky so often.
In the morning, in the evening, and at night.)
Where are we...?
